options.name: Centennial Park (Duncan Town Park cyclist camping)
options.priceNote: Town of Duncan officially lists 'long-distance cyclist camping' at Centennial Park; journals report free or small donation — confirm at Town Hall (928) 359-2791 (M–Th 8:00–5:30)
options.locationNote: On SE Old West Hwy (US 70) as the route passes through Duncan; coords approximate — you can't miss it in a town this size
options.legalityNote: Explicitly designated by the town for long-distance cyclist camping — fully legal
options.cyclistIntel: Classic Southern Tier overnight; park has restrooms, picnic kiosks, bandstand. Check in / say hi at Town Hall on arrival if open
options.seasonalNote: Pool showers (Veterans Park) are summer-only; late-Oct nights in the Gila valley can drop near freezing

options.name: Simpson Hotel B&B (indoor fallback, not camping)
options.priceNote: Rough estimate $95–135/room; not camping — the town's beloved cyclist-friendly B&B if weather turns
options.locationNote: Main St, Duncan, on route; coords approximate
options.cyclistIntel: Publishes its own local bike-route pages; well known to ST riders as the Duncan splurge option

bestBet: Centennial Park (Duncan Town Park cyclist camping)

options.name: Graham County Fairgrounds
options.priceNote: Rate not published online — estimate based on comparable AZ county fairgrounds; call (928) 428-7180 (fairgrounds) or Parks Office (928) 428-6240 to confirm price and tent policy
options.locationNote: 527 E Armory Rd, Safford — roughly 1 mi off US 70 between Safford and Thatcher; coords approximate
options.legalityNote: County-run RV/camping area with full-hookup back-in sites; tent acceptance unverified — call first
options.cyclistIntel: Fairgrounds are a standard budget fallback for tourers when state park is full
options.seasonalNote: May be unavailable during fair/event weekends

options.name: Roper Lake State Park (Cottonwood/Gila campgrounds)
options.priceNote: $25/night non-electric site + $3.60 non-refundable reservation fee (2025–26 AZ State Parks schedule); electric sites cost more
options.locationNote: ~3.6 mi off route (turn at mi 2148.5, S of Safford via US 191); short flat detour before the Thatcher day-end
options.legalityNote: Established state park campground — fully legal
options.cyclistIntel: 51 tent/RV sites, hot-spring soaking tub on site, showers — best real-shower night of this segment. Late Oct is snowbird season; reserving the $3.60 fee is worth it
options.seasonalNote: Open year-round; October weather at 3,100 ft is mild

options.name: Bylas church hosting (ask locally)
options.locationNote: Bylas town center on US 70, San Carlos Apache Reservation; several churches sit along/near the highway
options.legalityNote: Staying as an invited guest of a resident/church is the only clearly legal overnight in Bylas — there is no established campground, and camping on tribal land otherwise requires a permit valid only at designated recreation areas (none at Bylas)
options.cyclistIntel: A 2017 ST journal (Pedaling Pair) was invited indoors by a Bylas pastor who 'frequently hosts cyclists and other travelers'; other riders report asking at the police station. Mt Turnbull Market / gas station on US 70 for water and food

gapAdvice: Honest gap: Bylas has no legal established camping. The San Carlos Apache recreation permit (~$7–10/day; buy online at sancarlos.nagfa.net or via vendors; Recreation & Wildlife Dept (928) 475-2343) covers camping only at designated tribal recreation areas — none of which are on US 70 near Bylas — so roadside camping here is NOT legal even with a permit. Realistic plays: (1) call the Recreation & Wildlife Dept in advance and ask specifically about an overnight option for a through-cyclist; (2) arrive early and ask at a church or the police station — riders are regularly hosted; (3) restructure: ride Safford→Globe (~86 mi, gentle US 70 grades) in one day as most ST riders do, or split at Apache Gold Casino RV Park/hotel (~mi 2237, 5 mi east of Globe, tribal-owned, RV $45 and tent policy inconsistent — call (928) 475-7800 range numbers or book the hotel).

options.name: Round Mountain Park (Globe city park)
options.priceNote: Free if permitted — overnight camping is by local tolerance, not posted policy; check with City of Globe / Globe PD before setting up
options.locationNote: Trailhead park on the E edge of Globe off US 60/70; ~1 mi off route, coords approximate
options.legalityNote: Could NOT verify a formal overnight-camping policy — treat as ask-permission only; do not assume
options.cyclistIntel: Some tourer reports of overnighting at Globe parks with permission, but nothing recent/verifiable found

options.name: Cherry Flat Campground (Tonto NF)
options.priceNote: Free primitive site historically; no longer listed on the Globe Ranger District's current site list — status uncertain, call (928) 402-6200
options.locationNote: ~4.6 mi off route up Icehouse/Kellner Canyon (FR 112) with a steep dirt climb of well over 1,000 ft — NOT recommended on a loaded touring bike
options.legalityNote: Legal NF camping if the site is still open; dispersed camping in Tonto NF is also legal off forest roads
options.cyclistIntel: The climb makes this a poor value vs. in-town options

options.name: Gila County Fairgrounds RV Park
options.priceNote: $15/day published (add $10/day only if using horse facilities); tent acceptance unverified — call (928) 402-4368
options.locationNote: 900 E Fairground Rd, just off US 70 ~3 mi before downtown Globe — essentially on route as you arrive from Peridot
options.cyclistIntel: Cheapest verified-price bed-down in the Globe area
options.seasonalNote: Can fill/close during fair and event weekends

options.name: Gila County RV Park & Batting Range (downtown Globe)
options.priceNote: Estimate — tent rate not published; The Dyrt lists 3 tent sites plus grass tent space; call (928) 425-4653 to confirm
options.locationNote: 130 W Ash St, right in downtown Globe on route; walk to food/groceries
options.legalityNote: Established private RV park that takes tents — legal and normal
options.cyclistIntel: This is the 'RV park right next to downtown' where ST riders (e.g., Pedaling Pair 2017) camped; owner lives on-site; showers, laundry, wifi
options.seasonalNote: Lower section rebuilding after flooding; upper park open — 28 spaces

bestBet: Gila County RV Park & Batting Range (downtown Globe)
gapAdvice: All real options are in/around Globe (mi ~2240–2243), 6–9 mi before the mapped Miami endpoint — Miami itself has no legal camping, only a couple of motels. Plan to stop in Globe; the extra 6 mi to Miami is trivial to make up next morning. Oak Flat CG (free, Tonto NF) is on US 60 toward Superior — the route turns NORTH on AZ 188 before it, so it is NOT relevant unless you're detouring.

options.name: Indian Point Recreation Site (Tonto NF)
options.priceNote: Free — 'No fees are required for this site' per USFS; 14-day limit
options.locationNote: ~0.9 mi off AZ 188 via FR 60/FR 661 (A-Cross Rd) across Tonto Creek; USFS warns DO NOT cross Tonto Creek when flowing — check flow before committing; coords approximate
options.legalityNote: Legal free NF camping, open year-round, first-come
options.cyclistIntel: Carry water from Globe or the Roosevelt Lake Marina store — no potable water here
options.seasonalNote: Open year-round; access depends on Tonto Creek being dry/low (usually fine in late Oct)

options.name: Little Pine Flat dispersed area (Tonto NF)
options.priceNote: Likely free Tonto NF dispersed camping — could NOT verify with USFS; confirm with Tonto Basin RD (602) 225-5395
options.locationNote: OSM shows it on route at mi 2314.8, ~7 mi PAST the day-41 endpoint on AZ 188 toward Jake's Corner; coords very approximate
options.legalityNote: Dispersed camping is generally legal on Tonto NF land off forest roads (no Tonto Pass needed away from the lake fee corridor)
options.cyclistIntel: Only worth it if you want to bank miles past Tonto Basin; no facilities at all

options.name: Bermuda Flat Shoreline Area (Roosevelt Lake)
options.priceNote: Camping via Tonto Daily Pass: $8/day bought in advance at a vendor (Globe has several) or $12/day at the on-site fee machine; pass is per vehicle — a solo cyclist should carry one to be squarely legal
options.locationNote: Right on AZ 188 along the north shore, NW of Cholla — no detour
options.legalityNote: Legal first-come dispersed shoreline camping with the daily pass; 14-day limit; avoid wash bottoms (flash-flood risk)
options.cyclistIntel: Buy the $8 pass in Globe before leaving — saves $4 and hassle
options.seasonalNote: OPEN Feb 16–Nov 14 only (closes Nov 15 for wintering bald eagles) — Oct 31 is fine

options.name: Windy Hill Campground (Roosevelt Lake)
options.priceNote: $25/night single site (2025–26 USFS rate); campground fee replaces the Tonto Pass
options.locationNote: ~2 mi off AZ 188 via paved road, SE shore before the dam; coords approximate
options.legalityNote: Established NF campground, open year-round; first-come Apr–Oct, odd-numbered sites reservable on Recreation.gov Nov 1–Mar 15
options.cyclistIntel: Huge campground — space essentially guaranteed on Oct 31; potable water on site; 2017 ST riders camped here (were even waved in free as cyclists, though that's not an official policy)

options.name: Cholla Campground (Roosevelt Lake)
options.priceNote: $25/night single site (2025–26 USFS rate); fee replaces the Tonto Pass
options.locationNote: Right on AZ 188, north shore, ~11 mi before the mapped day-41 endpoint — plan to end the day here
options.legalityNote: Established NF campground with dedicated tent-only sites; even-numbered sites first-come, odd-numbered reservable Nov 1–Mar 15
options.cyclistIntel: The comfort pick: potable water, FLUSH toilets, and showers, directly on route
options.seasonalNote: Closed June 1–Oct 1 annually and shown 'Site Closed' in Aug 2026 (summer closure) — should be reopened by Oct 31, but CALL Tonto Basin RD (602) 225-5395 to confirm reopening before relying on it; Windy Hill is the confirmed-open backup

gapAdvice: All lake campgrounds sit 10–25 mi BEFORE the mapped 2307.5 endpoint — end the day at the lake (Cholla mi ~2295 or Bermuda Flat mi ~2297) rather than the abstract 'near Tonto Basin' point. Budget pick: Bermuda Flat at $8 if you carry water from Globe or the Roosevelt Lake Marina store. Schoolhouse Point was 'Temporarily Closed' as of Aug 2026. Verify Cholla's Oct 1 reopening by phone; Windy Hill (water, $25, confirmed open) is the fail-safe.

options.name: Usery Mountain Regional Park (Buckhorn Campground)
options.priceNote: $40/night developed site (all Buckhorn sites have water+electric) + $10 non-refundable reservation fee, per Maricopa County fee schedule effective Jan 1 2026 (rises to $50 in 2027); no primitive/semi-developed sites at Usery
options.locationNote: 3939 N Usery Pass Rd, NE Mesa — essentially on route at the base of Usery Pass, ~10–12 mi before the Gilbert endpoint
options.legalityNote: Established county regional park campground — legal and normal; the only real tent camping in metro east Phoenix
options.cyclistIntel: Standard last-camp-before-Phoenix for ST riders; showers, flush toilets, gorgeous Sonoran desert setting. Late Oct/Nov 1 is peak snowbird season — reserve online ahead
options.seasonalNote: Open year-round; Nov 1 weather is ideal

options.name: Mesa/Apache Junction KOA Journey
options.priceNote: Estimate ~$45–55 for a tent site — over budget and unverified for Nov 2026; all ages, tents accepted
options.locationNote: Apache Junction, ~6–7 mi SE of the route near the day-end — a detour, only as overflow
options.cyclistIntel: Only relevant if Usery is full; otherwise skip
options.seasonalNote: Snowbird season pricing in effect by Nov

gapAdvice: Metro Phoenix camping is genuinely awkward: Usery is the only sensible legal tent option and now runs $50 all-in ($40 + $10 reservation fee) after the Jan 2026 county fee hike — over the $35 cap but still the best move. Fiesta RV Resort at the Gilbert endpoint is a 55+ RV resort with no tents — excluded, as are the other age-restricted Mesa resorts. McDowell Mountain Regional Park is 25+ mi off-route (same $40 county rate) — not worth it. If $50 stings, budget motels on US 60/Main St in Mesa run ~$60–85 and Warmshowers hosts are plentiful in Mesa/Gilbert — for a shower, laundry, and real bed before the final push, a motel arguably beats the campground on value here.
